scenes.text: Imagine a fifty-square-mile strip of land in the United States where you could theoretically commit a major crime and legally walk free.
It sounds like a movie plot, but it is a real constitutional loophole in Yellowstone National Park because of how federal court districts are drawn.
If a crime happens in the Idaho section, the Constitution guarantees you a trial by a jury from that exact district, but absolutely nobody lives there to form a jury.
With no possible jury, a trial can never legally happen, so would you ever dare to visit this lawless zone? Let me know in the comments and follow for more!
